newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADA'S CHURCHILL PORT TO BE SOLD TO OMNITRAX.
newsitem.headline: CANADA'S CHURCHILL PORT TO BE SOLD TO OMNITRAX.

text.p: Canada's northern-most grain handling port will be sold to an affiliate of Denver-based OmniTRAX Inc later this month or in September, a Transport Canada spokeswoman said.
"(Federal) cabinet's agreed to it but funding still has to be approved by Treasury Board," Transport Canada spokeswoman Sheila Ryan-Monette said.

The governments of Canada and Manitoba agreed to spend C$34.05 million upgrading, dredging and repairing the port and harbor prior to the sale to OmniTRAX affiliate Hudson Bay Port Co, Transport Canada documents show.
Transport Canada was mandated in 1995 with divesting itself of sea and airport terminals.
Treasury Board, the federal agency that allocates government spending, will review the sale terms on August 28.

OmniTRAX's purchase of 850 km (528 miles) of a Canadian National Railway Co line from The Pas to Churchill and 350 km (218 miles) of a secondary line from The Pas to Lynn Lake pends approval of the port sale.
Churchill handled a yearly average 285,000 tonnes of wheat and barley for the Canadian Wheat Board over the past 10 years in its three month season, Transport Canada figures show.
The port has a maximum annual capacity of one million tonnes.
